query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The application of a protective coating can enhance the oxidation resistance of metal substrates.
generation.material_initial_state: Metal substrate exposed to oxidative environments.
generation.mechanism: The coating acts as a barrier, preventing oxygen and moisture from reaching the metal surface.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced oxidation rates and improved longevity of the metal substrate.
generation.baseline: Uncoated metal substrate exposed to the same oxidative conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to metals that can be effectively coated.
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the coating may vary based on the type of metal and coating material used.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare oxidation rates of coated and uncoated metal samples under identical oxidative conditions.
measurements: Surface analysis for oxide layer formation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples show no significant reduction in oxidation rates compared to uncoated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
